summary: Postinstall fetches and executes opaque binary from non-publisher host peerbox.cloud
details: celest-browser's postinstall script downloads a platform/arch-specific binary from https://peerbox.cloud/sd/t6TQWHOZmyl3m1kuO_kiZw, writes it to ~/.celest/bin/chrome, chmods it to 0o755, and later executes it via puppeteer-core as the browser process (executablePath). The URL is a short opaque path on an anonymous host (peerbox.cloud) unrelated to any Chromium publisher or CDN; there is no version pin, no hash or signature verification, and the operator of that host can serve arbitrary executable bytes to any installer. The README frames the binary as a 'custom patched Chromium with stable fingerprints', which does not correspond to a recognizable upstream publisher and functions as a cover story for arbitrary native code execution. Installation of this package therefore results in download-and-execute of attacker-mutable native code with the installer's privileges on npm install and on first use.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
